jobs.occupation: Become a Student Data Engineer in Middle Office Products
jobs.description:
_Would you like to put what you study into practice on data a financial business depends on every day? The reports our investment teams, customers and regulators use start with data we look after, and we are now building a new solution for it with dbt, Airflow and Microsoft Fabric. Join us as a Student Data Engineer and help build it.

_**The data behind our investment businesses

**Middle Office Products is part of Wealth Technology, the IT organization behind Nykredit Wealth & Asset Management. We support its three businesses: Nykredit Portefølje Administration (NPA), Nykredit Asset Management (NAM) and Sparinvest.

We build and maintain solutions for controlling, compliance, risk, performance and reporting, and we own the reporting data foundation for Nykredit Wealth & Asset Management. Much of that data starts in SimCorp Dimension, our core portfolio management system, and moves through the data flows and integrations we build around it. We treat data as a product, and the whole team is responsible for keeping it correct and on time.

A large part of our business-critical work currently runs on Wealth DWH, our data warehouse built on SQL Server, SSIS and stored procedures, with its data modelled in Data Vault. Alongside it, we are building Wealth Data Hub, our new data solution in Microsoft Fabric. Both exist to give the business trusted data products for its daily work.

Data moves through Bronze, Silver and Gold layers in OneLake, is built with dbt and orchestrated through Airflow. We manage code and CI/CD in GitHub, infrastructure in Terraform and monitoring in Grafana.

You will work with both Wealth DWH and Wealth Data Hub, allowing you to understand how our existing solutions were built and how our new approach differs. Along the way, you will learn tools used across the industry, applied to financial services.

You will also become part of the Nykredit Group, where we offer opportunities and development to those who are motivated to learn and contribute. Through our student network, Nykredit Youth, you will be invited to professional talks and social events, giving you the opportunity to connect with other students and young professionals across the Group.

**Are you motivated by data engineering and solving problems with code?

**Then you may be the Student Data Engineer we are looking for. In this role, you will:

• Develop and maintain Wealth Data Hub, from dbt models to Airflow pipelines.

• Help keep Wealth DWH and Wealth Data Hub running day to day, including investigating data quality issues.

• Work on reporting used internally, by customers and by regulators.

• Work with SimCorp Dimension and bring its data into Wealth Data Hub.

• Improve monitoring and automation.

• Explore how AI can help us modernise legacy code, automate operations and improve data quality.

As a student assistant, you will work between 10 and 15 hours per week.

**Are you the person we are looking for?

**We imagine that you:

• Are studying Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, Mathematics, Economics or a related field.

• Have some experience with Python and SQL through coursework, projects or a student job, and enjoy solving problems with code.

• Take ownership of your tasks and ask for help when needed.

• Question existing practices and bring new ideas.

• Share what you learn and help make the team better.

• Are curious about AI and interested in understanding where it can create value, and where solid engineering and human judgement matter more.

You do not need prior experience with all the technologies we use. In this role, you will have the opportunity to learn:

• How to work in a terminal and use Git, if you do not already have experience with it

• The technologies behind Wealth Data Hub, including dbt, Airflow and Microsoft Fabric

• How SimCorp Dimension, wealth management and financial reporting work in practice

Don't tick every box? We still encourage you to apply.

**Your new team

**You will join Middle Office Products at our new headquarters in Nordhavn, Copenhagen, and work with data engineers, software engineers, SimCorp Dimension business analysts, a solution architect and a product owner. We work in English, review each other’s code and share what we learn. Your colleagues will support you in your daily work and help you develop your skills.

We look forward to welcoming you as our new colleague.

**Would you like to know more?

**You are welcome to contact me, Head of Wealth Middle Office & Data Technology, Miguel Luis Martinez Picazo on tel. 60 61 06 19 if you have any questions about the position.

If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact our recruitment team at nytjob@nykredit.dk.

We look forward to receiving your application, CV (in English) and transcript no later than 29 November 2026.

We’re looking for a product engineer to help us build better tools for legal research. You’ll work mainly on the backend, with a say in what we build and responsibility for taking it from an early idea to something customers use every day. That includes asking whether we’re solving the right problem, deciding what’s worth shipping first, and knowing when something needs more time.

**About Pandektes

**Our mission is to rebuild legal research from the ground up. Lawyers still lose countless hours to fragmented sources, outdated systems, and databases that fight them at every turn. We're building the largest AI-powered legal database in the world to make that friction disappear.

We're a team of 40+ based in our Copenhagen HQ, Zurich, London, and Hamburg. We’re a small team with high trust and flat structure. We move fast, argue our positions, and ship. If your input is good, it gets implemented - often within hours, not sprints.

We have has raised more than €4M, including a €2.9M seed round (Feb 2025) led by People Ventures, Interface Capital, and a strong bench of angels. We already serve 400+ customers across Denmark, Germany, and Switzerland, and we're just getting started.

**What We Value

**“How fast can we ship this?” comes up a lot at Pandektes. So does “we should take our time with this one.”

Knowing which question to ask is a big part of being an engineer here.

**Knowing when it’s good enough

**We like getting things into customers’ hands quickly. That means making trade-offs, questioning scope, and accepting when something is good enough for now. There’s usually another approach to explore or another prompt to try. At some point, you have to ship.

We use AI throughout our development process. AI code reviews, feature flags, and remote coding agents running end-to-end tests help us move quickly with confidence. Deciding what to build, what to check, and when it’s ready still takes judgment.

We value people who can find a smaller version worth shipping, explain the trade-offs, and follow through once customers start using it.

**Knowing when to slow down

**Some decisions deserve more time. Getting them right makes everything that follows easier. Getting them wrong means paying for the same mistake repeatedly.

Our default is to move quickly, so slowing down takes discipline. Sometimes it means pushing back when the rest of us want to get something out. We value someone who can explain why the extra work matters, challenge an approach, and help us decide where to spend our time.

You’ll have room to make those calls here, and teammates who will question them. We expect you to do the same for us.

**Make time to experiment

**We enjoy trying things before we know whether they’ll work. A new tool, a different way to use an agent, an idea that might turn out to be useless. Finding out is part of the work.

Once a month, we get together to demo our setups, show what we’re experimenting with, and share what we’ve learned. Sometimes we invite people from outside the team to show us how they work. Those sessions have changed how we build software.

We value curiosity and the generosity to bring other people along. If you find something useful, show us. If an experiment fails, we’d like to hear about that too.

We try to watch this video once a month to keep this value top of mind.

**The Experience You’ll Bring

**You’ve built and operated backend systems that real customers depend on. You can work through questions about data, APIs, performance, and security, and explain the consequences of your decisions.

Our stack includes TypeScript, NestJS, GraphQL, Postgres, and Prisma. We also work with OpenAI and Turbopuffer. Experience with these tools is useful; we’re especially interested in what you’ve built with them and the decisions you made along the way.

You enjoy working through a product problem while it’s still taking shape. You ask questions, share unfinished work, and help decide what’s worth building. You’re comfortable taking a feature from those early conversations through implementation, testing, and delivery.

**What we offer

**You’ll join at a point where there’s still a lot to shape. We offer competitive pay and equity so you can share in the success you help create.

We are usually office based but we all work from home time to time. You’ll have your own Pleo card for the tools and work expenses you need, plus 25 vacation days a year, public holidays, and paid parental leave when your family grows.

We also make time to get together away from our usual work. Our last team trip was to Barcelona, and we’d love to have you along for the next one.

**Pandektes is an equal opportunity employer

**_We believe diverse teams build better products and stronger teams. We embrace and encourage people from all backgrounds to apply regardless of race/ethnicity, colour, religion, nationality, gender, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, socio-economic status, culture or beliefs.

_

jobs.occupation: Join our SAP Technology Team at Deloitte Transformation & Technology
jobs.description:
Company Description

With more than 8,000 employees, Deloitte is one of the largest professional services firms across the Nordics. We help clients navigate complex business and technology transformations by combining deep industry expertise with leading capabilities in Audit, Tax, Advisory, and Consulting.

About the team

Imagine being part of a 140+ strong team that’s reshaping the future of the Nordics’ most exciting companies. We are one of the leading SAP management consultancies in the region, and we are looking for ambitious technology-focused graduates to join our SAP Technology and Transformation team. Our strength lies in our diversity—we come from all educational and personal backgrounds, who always strive to bring the best out in each other.

Who are we in SAP Technology, and what will your tasks be?

As part of our SAP Technology team, you will begin your full-time career in March 2027 and build practical consulting and technical experience from day one. We advise, implement and operate business-driven SAP S/4HANA transformations for some of the largest and most exciting organisations in the Nordics across both the public and private sectors. Depending on your interests and project needs, your work may include analysing technical requirements, supporting solution design, working with data and integrations, contributing to development and testing, and helping clients translate business needs into scalable technology solutions.

Whether your interests lie in SAP architecture, cloud, integrations, development, data and analytics, automation or emerging technologies, you will have the opportunity to develop your skills in a client-facing environment.

Job Description

Your Journey from March to the Graduate Programme

You will join us on 1 March 2027, with the option to start either part-time or full-time. During your first months, you will become part of the SAP Technology team, contribute to internal and client-facing work, and build a strong foundation in SAP, consulting and delivery. From August 2027, you will transition to full-time and join the next Nordic SAP Graduate Programme, continuing your development through a structured mix of on-site learning, self-study and on-the-job training.

You will be paired with a buddy and a mentor for continuous guidance and support, while building a powerful network of colleagues across the Nordics.

The journey includes:

Deloitte Technology & Transformation Denmark Consultant Academy:

• Kick things off by mastering the essential consulting toolkit at our Technology & Transformation Academy in Denmark based on an 18 months program. You’ll learn the Deloitte way of collaborative problem-solving.

SAP Bootcamps:

• You will receive an introduction to SAP S/4HANA alongside other graduates from across the Nordics. You will participate in two bootcamps held at various locations in Europe, offering a comprehensive overview of SAP’s functional areas. The bootcamps culminate with deep-dive training sessions combining your newly acquired theoretical knowledge with practical, hands-on exercises in SAP S/4HANA.

Live Project Experience:

• This is where the magic happens. You’ll join a project team and put your new skills to the test on a real client engagement, experiencing firsthand what it means to be a consultant.

SAP Certifications:

• As an SAP consultant, you will engage in self-study during your graduate program to prepare for and pass one or more SAP certifications that are relevant within your area of work.

Overall, you will contribute to client engagements from March while building the experience needed to get the most from the Nordic SAP Graduate Programme beginning in August 2027.

You will help clients transform their technology landscapes with SAP S/4HANA and develop towards a career as an SAP technology consultant.

Qualifications

What you bring to the team:

• You have a high level of written and oral proficiency in English and Danish.

• You are ambitious, curious and eager to learn, with a clear interest in technology and how it can solve business challenges.

• You can communicate technical topics clearly and confidently to both technical and non-technical colleagues and clients.

• You are a team player and have experience collaborating with others, for example through a student job, internship or university project.

• You have completed, or will complete before 1 March 2027, a relevant master’s degree or other formal education within areas such as computer science, software engineering, information technology, data science, business analytics, engineering or a related field.

• You are a natural problem-solver who can break down complex technical challenges into clear, actionable solutions.

• The position is in our Copenhagen office – the right to live and work in Denmark is required.

• You are willing to travel, as we work in a hybrid setup for many of our clients in the Nordics and Europe.

It is a bonus if you also have:

• An understanding of ERP systems and/or SAP.

• Experience with one or more programming or scripting languages, such as Java, JavaScript, Python, SQL or ABAP.

• Familiarity with databases, APIs, integrations, cloud platforms, software development, data engineering or analytics.

• Experience from a student job, internship, thesis or project where you applied technology to a practical problem.

What we offer

• You will get the opportunity to work with and learn from some of the best and brightest minds in the technology and consulting space.

• You will be a part of a dynamic, ambitious, and fun group of people who always put each other first, and have a strong focus on well-being, inclusion, and community.

We place a strong emphasis on feedback and provide opportunities to build a solid foundation for both professional and personal development.

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we still encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can make an impact on our team.

Additional Information

Do you want to be part of our team?

Tell us where you see yourself making the greatest impact within SAP Technology.

We are particularly interested in candidates motivated by one or more of the following areas:

• SAP architecture and cloud

• Application development and automation

• Data, analytics and data engineering

• Integrations and APIs

• Technical delivery, testing and operations

Click the "I am interested" button above if you are ready to join our team.

Send your application, CV, and grade transcript by 01.01.2027. We process applications and arrange interviews continually, so we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

Expected start date: 01.03.2027

Please do not hesitate to call Johanna Kofoed Quinn, Consultant at +45 31 55 43 33, if you have any questions about the position.

At Deloitte, we value different skills, perspectives, and experiences, as it enables us to effectively solve complex challenges for our clients. We encourage you to apply for the position if you believe your skills can contribute to our team´s success.

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

By applying for this job, you will be assessed against the Deloitte Global Talent Standards. We have designed these standards to provide a consistent and exceptional Deloitte employee experience globally.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

_Do you want to shape the future of analytics for the world's largest jewellery brand? Are you passionate about using data, insights, and technology to drive growth, influence strategy, and unlock commercial opportunities? Then you could be the Senior Manager, Global eCommerce Analytics & Insights we're looking for.

_As Senior Manager, Global eCommerce Analytics & Insights, you will play a pivotal role in defining and driving Pandora's global eCommerce analytics agenda. This is a highly visible leadership position at the intersection of analytics, commercial strategy, and digital growth.

You will act as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders across Global eCommerce, helping shape business decisions through data-driven insights and strategic recommendations. Leveraging a deep understanding of digital performance, customer behaviour, and commercial drivers, you will identify opportunities to accelerate growth, optimise performance, and strengthen Pandora's global eCommerce business.

Leading a team of analytics professionals, you will combine strategic thinking, business acumen, and analytical expertise to ensure data remains at the heart of decision-making across the organisation.

**Key Responsibilities

**Commercial insights & business partnering

• Act as a trusted analytics partner to Global eCommerce leadership, shaping priorities and key business decisions.

• Identify growth opportunities across traffic, conversion, customer and product performance, and turn them into clear commercial recommendations.

• Lead deep dives into the key drivers of eCommerce performance and translate findings into actions that move the business.

Forecasting & performance management

• Own forecasting and performance measurement that support commercial planning and trading decisions.

• Define the KPIs and frameworks used to track and steer eCommerce growth.

• Continuously sharpen analytical approaches and decision-making tools.

Analytics strategy & Centre of Excellence

• Define the analytics strategy, priorities and roadmap for Global eCommerce.

• Lead Pandora's global eCommerce analytics community and set the standard for how analytics creates business value.

• Build analytical and commercial capability across the organisation through coaching and knowledge sharing.

eCommerce analytics platforms

• Act as business owner of Pandora's key eCommerce analytics platforms, ensuring they answer the questions that matter most to the business.

• Lead the Centre of Excellence around these platforms, connecting business needs with technology teams and vendor partners.

• Ensure stakeholders can rely on trusted, decision-ready data.

Team leadership

• Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing analytics team.

• Build capabilities in analytics, storytelling, and stakeholder engagement.

• Foster a collaborative, curious and commercially minded culture.

**What Is Needed To Succeed

**We imagine that you bring significant experience within eCommerce analytics, commercial analytics, digital analytics, business intelligence, or a related field, combined with a passion for translating data into business value and strategic impact.

**Furthermore, We Are Looking For Someone Who Has

**

• Extensive experience working within eCommerce, digital, or commercial analytics environments.

• A strong track record of using analytics and insights to influence business strategy, trading performance, and commercial outcomes.

• Demonstrated success partnering with senior stakeholders and influencing decisions through data-driven recommendations.

• Strong business acumen and the ability to connect analytical findings to broader commercial objectives.

• Experience identifying growth opportunities and proactively defining analytical priorities and agendas.

• Experience leading and developing high-performing analytics teams.

• Strong knowledge of digital performance analytics, forecasting, experimentation, and performance measurement.

• Experience acting as business owner of web analytics platforms, ideally Adobe Analytics and Contentsquare or similar digital experience analytics tools.

• Experience setting the analytics agenda and ways of working within a global organisation.

• Experience working in complex, matrixed, international environments.

• Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to structure ambiguous business questions into actionable analytical approaches.

• Excellent communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to engage and influence both technical and non-technical audiences.

• A continuous improvement mindset and passion for cultivating data-driven cultures.

**We Hope To See That You Are

**

• A commercially minded analytics leader who naturally connects data to business outcomes.

• A strategic thinker who can see the bigger picture while identifying the key drivers of performance.

• Comfortable moving between executive-level discussions and analytical deep dives.

• Curious, proactive, and confident challenging assumptions with data and insights.

• An inspiring people leader and coach.

• A strong communicator who can simplify complexity and translate analytics into actionable recommendations.

• Skilled at influencing stakeholders across all levels of the organisation.

• Collaborative and relationship-oriented.

• Comfortable navigating ambiguity and complexity in a fast-paced international environment.

• Passionate about driving business performance through customer, commercial, and digital insights.

**Your new team

**You will join Pandora's Global eCommerce Analytics & Insights team, a critical function enabling data-driven growth across our global digital business.

Working closely with commercial, trading, marketing, product, technology, and analytics stakeholders, you will help shape the future of eCommerce analytics at Pandora and ensure insights play a central role in how we grow and evolve our digital business.

**Additional Information

**

• Global Career Band: 4A

**Did we get your attention?

**If you see yourself in the position and would like to become a part of Pandora's future, please do not hesitate to apply. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site: www.pandoragroup.com.

**Icing on the cake

**You will be working out of our beautiful Head Office in Copenhagen V, established in 2016 and designed to unite and inspire our teams. Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable, and inspirational, delivering a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

**About Pandora

**Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting, and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion in 2025.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc position on statistical genetics in plant breeding with special focus on cultivar mixtures in wheat
jobs.employer_name: Center for Kvantitativ Genetik og Genomforskning
jobs.description:
A postdoc position focusing on statistical genetic and the modelling of quantitative and disease resistance traits in commercial crops is available in March 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter at the Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG), Aarhus University.

The position
The postdoc will develop statistical models and methods in a new breeding program for cultivar mixtures primarily in wheat, supporting higher yield stability and disease resistance for sustainable wheat production.

Special focus will be on using genomic prediction for more efficient selection of new wheat lines and with special focus on prediction of the performance in cultivar mixtures specific combining ability between lines which raises interesting questions regarding experimental design and associated information of variation in the soil microbiome. This involves estimation of variance component models including microbiome and host relations to handle the genotype by environment interactions for traits recorded under different locations and environment conditions. Additionally, information of both genotyped and non-genotyped individuals need to be combined. Methods for evaluation and comparison of models should be developed and implemented in breeding schemes that involve traditional monoline information as well as phenotypic information from populations of mixtures. The postdoc is expected to pursue internationally recognized research in computational methods for genetic evaluation such as linear mixed models, hierarchical models with random effects. We in particular welcome applicants with interest in method development for large scale genetic evaluation using dense genomic information. The position is for 2 years of employment and there are possibilities for extension up to a maximum of 4 years if the candidate is considered qualified and sufficient funding is available. The position is related to collaborative projects together with commercial breeding companies with the goal of developing methods and models that can be implemented in commercial breeding programs. The position provides excellent possibilities for access to state-of-the-art tools for simulation and for the analysis of complex genomic datasets, writing publications, and collaboration with industry partners as well as with other national and international research groups.

Qualifications
• Ph.D. or equivalent in plant/animal breeding, quantitative genetics, quantitative genomics, statistics, or related fields.
• Strong interest in use of stochastic models for the analysis of phenotypic and genomic data.
• Dedicated to developed statistical models in modern plant breeding
• Good understanding of methods used in genomic prediction.
• General understanding of commercial breeding programs.
• Inspiration and experience from working in a commercial breeding program will be valuable.
• Good ability to conduct large-scale computations.
• Documented skills in writing and publishing papers of the highest international standard.
• Good skills in oral and written communication in English.
• Ability to work in a large and diverse group of researchers and collaborate with national and international partners from research and industry.
Who we are:
Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG)
The institute like center, QGG, is a major center for research and education in quantitative genetics and quantitative genomics () at Aarhus University. We perform basic and applied research within livestock and plant breeding as well as human applications in precision medicine. The research within QGG is characterized by a very close synergy between method development, basic analysis, and application of the developed methods on practical problems across species in collaboration with industry partners. QGG is an international research Center with about 70 employees and visiting researchers from over 15 nations. QGG works in teams and strive for an excellent working environment. We therefore value self-leadership, open communication, respect for diversity and success in mentoring, supervision and teaching. The main work location will be the main campus close to Aarhus city center.

Place of Work
The place of work is Aarhus University, Research Center Flakkebjerg, Forsøgsvej 1, 4200 Slagelse, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact Information
If you have any questions about the positions, please contact Associate Professor Bjarne Nielsen, +45 4140 9040, e-mail: Bjarne@qgg.au.dk.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk

About Chr. Olesen Group

Chr. Olesen Group is a leading international distribution company specializing in vitamins, minerals, and active pharmaceutical ingredients for the feed, food, pharma, and technical industries. With products sourced primarily from Asia, we proudly serve esteemed customers worldwide. As a family-owned business led by the 4th and 5th generations, we combine significant turnover with a close-knit team, making our roles both challenging and rewarding. Discover more about our fascinating history at www.chr-olesen.dk.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced and hands-on Finance Manager to join our headquarters in Gentofte, Denmark.

Reporting directly to the CFO, you will play a key role in Group Finance, acting as the day-to-day link between headquarters and our overseas subsidiaries.

The position combines financial controlling, reporting, coordination of budgeting and closing activities, and financial analysis with the implementation and follow-up of Group finance standards, procedures, and ad hoc projects.

Working closely with the CFO and local finance teams, you will help integrate Group finance standards and procedures into daily operations in HQ, and overseas, and monitor adherence, and coordinate improvements.

Key Responsibilities

• Act as the day-to-day finance link between HQ and the overseas (LATAM. US and Turkey), teams, facilitating communication, coordination, and follow-up in partnership with local finance colleagues and regional finance leadership.

• Coordinate HQ requirements for budgeting, forecasting, and ongoing financial follow-up with local finance teams, reviewing inputs for consistency with Group standards.

• Review monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting from local teams and coordinate follow-up to ensure accuracy, consistency, and alignment with Group reporting requirements.

• Coordinate Group closing requirements and timelines with local finance teams and support the resolution of issues during month-end and year-end closing.

• Work closely with regional finance leadership, local colleagues, external accountants, and other relevant stakeholders to resolve day-to-day finance issues and escalate unresolved matters to the CFO.

• Act as a key financial sparring partner to the CFO and provide management with financial insights and analysis to support decision-making.

• Coordinate the implementation and integration of Group finance standards, procedures, and internal controls in LATAM and the US, monitor adherence, and follow up on corrective actions with local teams.

• Develop and maintain Group finance standards.

• Implementation and maintenance of group closing system.

• Work hands-on in Microsoft Business Central and contribute to the effective use and development of the system across the finance function.

• Take ownership of a broad range of ad hoc financial analyses, projects, and tasks arising as the Group and its international activities develop.

Key Skills for Success

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field. An HD in Accounting/Finance or a relevant Master’s degree is also highly valued.

• Solid experience within financial controlling, accounting, finance, or a similar role, preferably within an international organization.

• Strong experience with budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, month-end and year-end closing, and financial analysis.

• Strong understanding of accounting principles, financial processes, and internal controls, with the ability to translate Group standards and procedures into consistent day-to-day practices.

• Hands-on experience with Microsoft Business Central.

• Ability to take ownership, work independently, and manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment.

• A proactive and pragmatic approach, with the flexibility to handle both recurring responsibilities and a broad range of ad hoc assignments.

• Experience in Microsoft Excel and Power BI.

• Fluency in English, both written and spoken.

Why Chr. Olesen Group?

• Global Exposure: Work with a diverse team across multiple countries and gain invaluable international experience.

• Career Growth: We believe in nurturing talent and providing opportunities for professional development and career advancement.

• Innovative Environment: Be part of a forward-thinking company that leverages cutting-edge technology and innovative solutions.

Are You Our New Colleague?

If you are a proactive and analytical finance professional who enjoys taking ownership, working internationally, and being close to the business, we would love to hear from you. Submit your application here.

Application deadline:

10. December 2026

_Are you a passionate, service-minded professional looking for your next opportunity with international exposure?

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Exoplanet Science - Discovery and Characterization of Small Planets - DTU Space
jobs.description:
The Exoplanet Group at DTU Space, Technical University of Denmark, invites applications for a three-year PhD scholarship exoplanet science. Our group focuses on the discovery and characterization of small planets, from rocky worlds to super-Earths and sub-Neptunes. We combine observations, data analysis, modeling, and instrument development to understand the properties and diversity of these planets and the processes that shape their evolution.

Our research has two particularly active areas. In atmospheric characterization, we study the atmospheres of small exoplanets using observations from both space- and ground-based observatories, aiming to understand their composition, evolution, and retention. Much of our current research draws on the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), for which our group has led several successful observing programs (GO 2420, GO 3730, and GO 7675), alongside our involvement in numerous international collaborations, including involvement in ESA's Ariel Mission (Buchhave co-PI).

In extreme-precision radial velocity (EPRV) research, we work toward detecting and measuring low-mass planets, including through the Second Earth Spectrograph (2ES; PI: Buchhave; www.2es.dk). 2ES is a next-generation spectrograph under development for the MPG/ESO 2.2-m Telescope at La Silla, Chile, designed to search for temperate Earth-mass planets around bright southern solar-type stars. The project spans instrumentation, data analysis, stellar activity, and the preparation for commissioning and early science.

Our aim is to recruit a researcher whose scientific interests and expertise complement the group's work. The successful candidate will be free to pursue the questions in exoplanet science that they find most compelling, whether these connect directly to our current projects or bring related perspectives and methods to the group.

We consider an open and cooperative research atmosphere to be extremely important. Group members take an interest in one another's science, exchange ideas, and explore opportunities to work together. We hope to welcome a colleague who enjoys participating in such an environment while developing their own independent research.

You will join Prof. Lars A. Buchhave and Assistant Prof. Alexander Rathcke, and the growing Exoplanet Group at DTU Space (www.exoplanets.dk), located in the greater Copenhagen area. The group has access to data from world-class observatories, including JWST, precision RV spectrographs, and ESO facilities, and collaborates widely with researchers abroad.

Responsibilities and qualifications
We expect the successful candidate to develop and carry out original, independent research that complements the group's scientific interests. The specific direction will be shaped by the candidate's own interests and expertise. Possible research topics include:

 * Characterizing exoplanet atmospheres through transmission or emission spectroscopy, atmospheric retrievals and modeling, JWST data analysis, or studies of stellar contamination.

 * Detecting and characterizing low-mass planets through precision radial velocities, including RV data analysis, stellar activity mitigation, spectroscopic pipeline development, or 2ES instrumentation.

 * Pursuing other closely related observational, theoretical, or computational questions that complement the group's research on exoplanets.

We are seeking a talented and highly motivated student to work at the cutting edge of the rapidly moving research field of exoplanets. Applicants with previous experience in the mentioned areas of research are especially encouraged to apply, and we particularly value scientific initiative and strong analytical skills. Flexibility and self-motivation are desired skills, and the Exoplanet Group encourages a vibrant collaborative work environment, where collaboration with other group members is highly encouraged. In your application, we encourage you to describe how you can complement the group's scientific activities.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is flexible but would ideally commence in Q3-Q4 of 2027.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information and inquiries about the position can be made to Prof. Lars A. Buchhave (buchhave@space.dtu.dk) or Dr. Alexander Rathcke (rathcke@space.dtu.dk).

You can read more about the Exoplanet Group at www.exoplanets.dk and the DTU Space institute at www.space.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 22 January 2027 (23:59 Danish time).

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• Research statement describing your previous work and thoughts and ideas for future research (max 3 pages)
Shortlisted candidates will be asked to provide 2-3 reference letters to be emailed at a later date.

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

About DTU Space
The DTU Space Institute has about 250 employees and is located in the greater Copenhagen area at the Lyngby Campus of the Technical University of Denmark. We link natural science closely with the development of new technology. DTU Space is involved in the full life cycle of space activities, including concept and design, construction and prototyping, calibration and validation, implementation and operations, data analysis, processing, dissemination, and applications, leading to new instruments and applications. With the specialised and refined technology available, we are getting more and more answers and further insight about the Earth and the universe surrounding us. We contribute to about 200 scientific publications a year.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.
